subject.title: fix: models status auth, browser local-file nav, codex workspace app-server, tui empty sessions

question: Should OpenClaw's Codex app-server workspace-write mode grant network egress by default, or remain network-denied unless an explicit opt-in/product path enables it?
rationale: The PR changes a security-sensitive default that affects existing app-server users and differs from upstream Codex's default workspace-write sandbox behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Keep workspace-write network-denied by default
options.body: Preserve the current default and require an explicit opt-in or separate maintainer-approved product path for workspace-write network egress.

options.title: Accept network egress as the new default
options.body: Merge the broader default only with maintainer-owned security rationale, upgrade notes, and proof that existing users are expected to receive network access.

options.title: Split the PR first
options.body: Land the TUI/browser/auth repairs separately and hold the sandbox policy change for a focused security/product review.

recommendation.title: Keep workspace-write network-denied by default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current default and require an explicit opt-in or separate maintainer-approved product path for workspace-write network egress.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior feature-history evidence connects this person to both browser security and auth scoping surfaces, and the sandbox choice needs the same security-boundary judgment.
